primitives.name: Dev Fake Admin Bypass
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Dev-admin bypass — `apps/web/lib/auth.ts` + `apps/web/middleware.ts` When `DEV_FAKE_ADMIN=true`: - `auth()` returns a synthetic ADMIN session (no DB hit).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a middleware architecture that intercepts authentication requests. Assumes the presence of an `auth()` function that normally interacts with a user database.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The regime involves a deliberate deviation from standard authentication flows, introducing a hard-coded override that skips the database lookup entirely.

layer2.mapping: This implements a form of quick failover used in A/B testing frameworks. By returning a fixed, synthetic session, it isolates the application logic from the auth service, similar to how a fallback handler operates in distributed systems.
layer2.telemetry: Metrics include the invocation frequency of the fake admin path and the response time of the `auth()` call compared to a real user lookup.

primitives.name: Environment Recovery Procedure
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## What I changed in this pass ### Environment recovery - `mv` (not `rm`) the corrupt `node_modules`, `_speedtest`, and `.git/index.lock` out of the way — Linux ACL accepted rename but rejected unlink.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a POSIX-compliant shell with file move capabilities. Assumes the existence of a corrupted file system state requiring manual intervention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The regime is one of manual cleanup following a permission-based locking failure, transitioning from a blocked state to a recoverable one.

layer2.mapping: This procedure maps to a state-machine reset pattern. Moving files rather than deleting them preserves the optionality for later analysis, akin to moving artifacts to a quarantine directory in software deployment.
layer2.telemetry: Key metrics are the time taken to complete the move operation and the success rate of subsequent npm installs post-recovery.

primitives.name: Cockpit Launch Observatory
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Middleware skips the cookie check on `/dashboard` and `/admin` so it does not 307 to `/auth/signin` before the page even runs.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a web framework with middleware that processes HTTP requests. Assumes the presence of authentication cookies and redirect rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The regime involves conditional request routing based on URL patterns, effectively creating a bypass for specific paths during early development.

layer2.mapping: This implements a pre-flight check mechanism common in API gateways. By skipping authentication for known safe routes, it reduces latency and prevents feedback loops, similar to how load balancers handle health probes.
layer2.telemetry: Observables include the number of redirects suppressed per minute and the average response time for dashboard requests.
